contexts.MG:
Here, I noticed something.
...I was contradicting myself.
I was strangling my own neck.
I want to deny Beatrice no matter what.
I want to erase the existence of that brutal, fickle, ridiculous witch!
So, I have to explain everything with humans, not magic.
...But that also means suspecting some human.
I don't want to suspect anyone.
...Of course, if there's some clear proof, I'll have to believe that the person in question is the culprit,
...but until that happens, I don't want to suspect people.
Am I just naive...?
Am I just a kid who doesn't want to have my feelings betrayed, when those feelings tell me that this person at least could never commit murder...?
contexts.UP:
At this point, I noticed something.
......I'm contradicting myself.
I'm cutting my own throat.
I want to deny Beatrice no matter what.
I want to erase the existence of that brutal, fickle, ridiculous witch!
In order to do that, I have to explain everything with humans, not magic.
......But that also means suspecting some human.
I don't want to suspect someone.
......Of course, if there was some clear proof, I would have to believe that person was the culprit,
...but as long as that didn't happen, I didn't want to cast any suspicions.
Am I just green...?
Am I just a kid who doesn't want to have my feelings, which tell me that at least this person or that person couldn't be a murderer, betrayed...?

UP.translation: I don't want to suspect someone. ......Of course, if there was some clear proof, I would have to believe that person was the culprit, ...but as long as that didn't happen, I didn't want to cast any suspicions.

findings.sourceReading: Battler recognizes his contradiction: he must seek a human explanation, but presently refuses to suspect a person unless clear evidence compels him.
findings.alternative: The surrounding present-tense monologue makes his continuing attitude recoverable. The two past forms nevertheless recast the condition and reluctance as earlier states.
